skill.name: neon-postgres
skill.description: Guidance for building Neon serverless Postgres setups with pooling, branch workflows, and Prisma or Drizzle integration patterns.
skill.summary: Plan Neon Postgres connections, pooling, migrations, and ORM driver choices for serverless apps.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a documentation reference to DATABASE_URL in SKILL.md. I treated it as a false positive because the skill does not access environment variables, request secrets, or include code that could exfiltrate credentials. No prompt injection or other semantic security issues were found.

static_findings.snippet: - DATABASE_URL: Pooled connection for Prisma Client

finding_verdicts.reason: The line names DATABASE_URL as a configuration label in documentation and does not read, request, transmit, or expose a secret. The skill gives connection-string separation guidance without code or credential collection.

content.value_statement: Serverless Postgres setups can fail when pooling, migrations, and ORM drivers are chosen incorrectly. This skill gives practical Neon patterns for Prisma, Drizzle, PgBouncer, and connection string separation.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use pooled and direct Neon connection strings.
Describes PgBouncer pooling limits and connection tradeoffs.
Compares Drizzle neon-http and neon-serverless driver choices.
Guides Prisma Client and Prisma Migrate connection setup.
Highlights migration workflows that need direct database connections.
limitations: Does not provision Neon projects or branches automatically.
Does not validate live database credentials or network access.
Does not replace current Neon, Prisma, or Drizzle documentation.
Does not include complete application code or schema migrations.

use_cases.title: Prepare Prisma Deployment
use_cases.description: Configure pooled and direct connection roles before deploying a Prisma-backed app on Neon.

use_cases.title: Choose Drizzle Driver
use_cases.description: Select the Neon Drizzle driver that matches serverless queries, sessions, and transactions.

use_cases.title: Review Connection Pooling
use_cases.description: Assess when PgBouncer pooling helps serverless traffic and when direct connections remain required.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Connection URLs
prompt_templates.prompt: I am new to Neon Postgres. Explain when I should use pooled and direct connection strings for Prisma.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Drizzle Driver
prompt_templates.prompt: For a serverless app on Neon, compare the Drizzle HTTP and WebSocket drivers for my workload: [describe workload].

prompt_templates.title: Plan Migration Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Neon Prisma deployment plan and identify where Prisma Client, Prisma Migrate, pooled connections, and direct connections should be used.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Scaling Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Neon Postgres architecture for pooling, migration, and serverless connection risks. Provide prioritized fixes and questions to verify.

output_examples.input: I need Prisma with Neon in a serverless app.
output: Use the pooled endpoint for application queries.
Use the direct endpoint for migrations.
Keep credentials in environment variables and avoid sharing real secrets.

output_examples.input: Should I use the Drizzle HTTP or WebSocket driver?
output_examples.output: Use the HTTP driver for simple one-off queries. Use the WebSocket driver when sessions or transactions are required.

output_examples.input: My app may receive traffic spikes on Neon.
output: Use PgBouncer pooling for high client concurrency.
Keep migrations on the direct connection path.

best_practices: Use separate pooled and direct URLs for app queries and migrations.
Choose the Drizzle driver based on transactions, sessions, and runtime constraints.
Keep real Neon credentials outside prompts, logs, and shared examples.
anti_patterns: Do not run migrations through a PgBouncer pooled endpoint.
Do not assume 10,000 pooled clients equal 10,000 database backends.
Do not paste production database URLs into chat prompts or issue trackers.

faq.question: Does this skill manage Neon accounts?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance and setup patterns only.

faq.question: Why should I use two connection strings?
faq.answer: Pooled URLs fit app traffic. Direct URLs are needed for migration operations that require DDL support.

faq.question: Is this skill useful for Prisma projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Prisma Client pooling and Prisma Migrate direct connections.

faq.question: Does this skill cover Drizzle ORM?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains HTTP and WebSocket driver choices for Neon serverless environments.

faq.question: Can I share my database URL in prompts?
faq.answer: Avoid sharing real credentials. Use redacted examples when asking for help.

faq.question: Does this replace official Neon documentation?
faq.answer: No. It is a concise guide. Verify provider limits and features against current official documentation.
